description:
We are GeoAI Space Explorers, a team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Kénitra, Morocco.

Our interests include geomatics, GIS, remote sensing, Earth observation, and satellite data analysis. We aim to use NASA open data to develop an innovative solution to a real-world challenge.

We are looking for motivated team members with skills in coding, data analysis, AI, web development, and graphic design. Beginners who are eager to learn and collaborate are welcome!
summary: AgriTrend AI is an interactive Earth observation and statistical trend-detection platform built to transform complex NASA satellite data into actionable agricultural intelligence. Addressing the "Be an Earth System Trend Detective" challenge, our tool empowers students, researchers, and farmers to investigate what is changing, where, by how much, and whether those changes are statistically significant.Using Google Earth Engine and NASA datasets (MODIS NDVI, GPM, SMAP, and NASA POWER), the platform generates multi-year time series and applies rigorous statistical tests—including Mann-Kendall, Sen’s Slope, and Linear Regression—to distinguish true climate trends from normal seasonal variations.   Demonstrated through a live case study of Morocco’s Gharb agricultural region, AgriTrend AI goes beyond historical detection by offering a 2026–2027 predictive crop-suitability module. It evaluates agro-environmental zones to recommend optimal crops (such as wheat, maize, lentils, chickpeas, potatoes, tomatoes, carrots, and sugar beet), making global NASA Earth science practical, accessible, and locally impactful.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

AgriTrend AI bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and real-world decision-making by turning users into "Earth System Trend Detectives." Built on Google Earth Engine (GEE)and integrated into a user-friendly web interface, the platform operates in three core stages:

  1. Guided Variable Selection & Simplification: Users explore key environmental variables—Vegetation Health (MODIS NDVI), Precipitation (NASA GPM), Surface Soil Moisture (NASA SMAP), and Temperature (NASA POWER)—accompanied by clear, jargon-free definitions designed for students and non-specialists.
  2. Historical Time-Series & Statistical Significance Engine: By clicking any location on the map (or selecting our primary demo in Morocco's Gharb region), the system extracts multi-year satellite time series (1982–2025)and automatically computes Kendall’s Tau, p-values, Sen’s Slope, and Linear Trendlines. This tells the user immediately whether an observed environmental shift is statistically significant ($p < 0.05$) or normal seasonal variability.
  3. 2026–2027 Predictive Crop Suitability & Agro-Environmental Zoning: Extending our analysis into practical forecasting (tested from November 2026 through late 2027), the application maps agro-environmental zones and evaluates crop suitability across 11 major crops—including wheat, barley, maize, chickpea, lentil, fava bean, potato, tomato, carrot, sugar beet, and sunflower.

Benefits & Intended Impact While demonstrated on the Gharb agricultural plain in Morocco—a vital agricultural hub facing climate variability—AgriTrend AI is scalable to any region across Morocco and the globe thanks to NASA's global Earth observation coverage. It empowers high school and university students to learn applied data science while helping farmers and planners adapt sowing schedules and crop choices to changing climate realities.

Tools, Data & Technologies Used

  • Cloud Geospatial Processing: Google Earth Engine (JavaScript API)
  • NASA Datasets: MODIS (MOD13Q1 NDVI), GPM (IMERG Precipitation), SMAP (Soil Moisture), and NASA POWER.
  • Statistical Methods: Mann-Kendall Trend Test, Sen’s Slope Estimator, and Ordinary Least Squares Linear Regression.
  • Frontend & Web Integration: Interactive web application integrating GEE Apps, dynamic charts, and spatial map layers.

Creativity & Design Considerations Our team focused on preventing false conclusions by explicitly warning users when a visual decline is not statistically significant ($p \ge 0.05$) and reminding them that statistical correlation does not automatically prove causation. Combining historical statistical rigor with forward-looking 2026–2027 crop suitability makes the platform both scientifically sound and immediately useful.
